description.value: The study examined whether intravenous ghrelin modulates neural responses to visual food cues in healthy men and whether these responses relate to hunger and memory for food images.

spans.text: Here, we show that ghrelin administered intravenously to healthy volunteers during functional magnetic resonance imaging increased the neural response to food pictures in regions of the brain, including the amygdala, orbitofrontal cortex, anterior insula, and striatum, implicated in encoding the incentive value of food cues.

design.value: Single-session fMRI study with a control/ghrelin group scanned before and after intravenous ghrelin and a separate control/control group scanned twice without ghrelin.

spans.text: Twelve subjects viewed pictures before and after ghrelin administration (control/ghrelin group), and eight subjects viewed the same pictures in two identical blocks without receiving ghrelin (control/control group).
At the start and end of the block, subjects answered questions regarding their mood and appetite (e.g., how hungry are you right now?) on a 10 point visual analog scale.
